comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD reported substantial year-over-year growth in their Data Center segment revenues for fiscal year 2024, driven by artificial intelligence and accelerated computing demand. However, the scale and growth rate differed significantly: NVDA's Data Center revenue grew 217% to $47.5 billion, while AMD's grew 94% to $12.6 billion. NVDA explicitly estimates that approximately 40% of this revenue was for AI inference, whereas AMD attributes its growth primarily to higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs, along with higher operating income.

sentences.text: Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2024 was $47.5 billion, up 217% from fiscal year 2023.
We estimate that in fiscal year 2024, approximately 40% of Data Center revenue was for AI inference.
Data Center net revenue of $12.6 billion in 2024 increased by 94%, compared to net revenue of $6.5 billion in 2023.
The increase was primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs.
